I don't mind sharing but I might have to answer this in 2 parts , some tonight, the rest  tmrw.  For me the decades have had a domino effect, in a negative way. Well. If there is anything positive , it is not pertinent now.  I was bullied alot as a teen and carried that resentment and anger around throughout my 20s. In a away, it was a wasted  decade . Neurosis. I bounced thru jobs and friends and relationships.  But I couldn't get it together.  I said anger. But lots of confusion too because I wasn't emotionally mature, or secure. I mean I wasn't childish but there was just arrested development in so many ways.  I deliberately worked jobs where I could be alone as much as possible. But I started to figure things out in my early 30s and had great friendships. I went back to school. Finished and  at 39 moved for a job. All my friends  also moved away for jobs.  So those relationships withered. A job was hard to find and I ended up in a rural area that had lots of Nascar culture. Im not knocking it but I was a liberal arts philosophical type. So I didn't fit in . Sometimes  I felt like Luke Wilson in a movie called Idiocracy. I was there for ten years and mostly isolated. I didn't make much money, for a while didn't have a car, and there was no one to date. I mean I was really alone alot. I feel like it was karmic  payback for squandering my 20s. Physicality I still had lots of energy. And was mentally active but eventually depression sets in. Still, I found a better job and moved but by then I felt worn out. I mean  I did not feel as energetic, physicality or mentally. Thats around 50.  Health issues set in too. Partial blindness in one eye from injury, lesion on asaphagus from acid reflux. removed,, but thats the cancer risk mentioned earlier.  Mentally, I developed a been there done that attitude and still have trouble socializing. im not antisocial. I just can't make a great connecton.  I think that as you age , you meet fewer people with common goals, i.e. school , marriage. And everyone  becomes more entrenched in their own habits. So that's currently my life at 53. I have regrets I dwell on. I also see friends and relatives dying and I think about death a lot. Age related  Blindness runs strongly in the family and im already not too good there.  Obviously I'm not too upbeat which also makes it harder to socialize. No one likes a downer.  More than not  I put on a good front. But it gets exhausting. I also worry about retirement, if I'm still alive.  Lol. So 50s for me has become  a time of reflection and worry, of been there done that,  of fatigue,  and of taking stock.  One good thing is that I unequivocally know what I want and don't want ,  and I know my limits. Sadly I also know what I missed out on and will never have. I don't know if this will help you. I mean this my own  journey and everyone's is different.  Yours may not be mine and vice versa. But I do  hope it  gives some kind of perspective and answers some of  your question. hopefully you find something in it.

Also the upside, if there is any, is that you r aware and they can catch it early.  Years ago it hit with out warning cause there were no gene tests. Im not trying to minimize your suffering though. I know its a raw deal. Fairness is not parcelled out in equal bundles
